text:
anya: Heads up — seeing intermittent NaNs + a 25–40% perf regression when the kernel switchover kicks in on the KV-hot path. Happens with fp8 + our dynamic eps schedule, mostly on long contexts (>1024). Repro on stage.
kevin: Oof. Do we have a tiny repro script? sounds like numerical stability + scheduling interaction.
mike: I ran a quick job this morning. Logs show softmax returning NaN around the switchover boundary and latency spikes right after.
anya: Minimal policy snippet we're using on stage:
```
kernel_policy:
  - condition: seq_len > 512 and kv_hot == true
    kernel: flash-attn-v2
    eps_schedule: dynamic
quant: fp8
eps_init: 1e-5
eps_max: 1e-2
hysteresis_ms: 40
```
mike: Perf diff from the run (same model, same batch):
```
before switchover (paged-attn): p50 18ms, p95 45ms
after switchover (flash-attn-v2): p50 24ms, p95 68ms
kernel time breakdown (ms): paged-attn=40, flash-attn-v2=60, kv-lock=5
```
mike: Log excerpt where NaNs show up:
```
[WARN] 2025-11-02T09:17:23Z step=2034 seq=512 softmax: output contains NaN
tensor-check: q_norm contains Inf at idx 110
stack: flash_attn_forward -> softmax_kernel -> exp_kernel
```
kevin: Two axes here: (1) fp8 quantization interacts poorly with extremely small eps, (2) switchover/hysteresis timing creates a mixed-batch boundary where inputs have different scaling. Both can expose exp overflow/underflow/Inf propagation.
kevin: Quick triage steps I recommend:
  - force eps to a fixed sane value (e.g., 1e-3) and rerun
  - disable fp8 for the switchover policy (fallback to bf16) to see if NaNs disappear
  - temporarily remove hysteresis so kernel isn't switching mid-request
anya: I tried fixing eps=1e-3 locally — NaNs stopped in my mini repro but perf still a bit worse than paged-attn. So numerical errors are part of it but there's a kernel performance regression too.
mike: I pushed a tiny instrumentation patch that prints per-request kernel decision and scaling constants. Added trace id 0x7f3 to noisy logs.
deploy-bot: kernel-policy rollout: flash-attn-v2 -> 2025-11-01T22:00:00Z -> rollout id rp-884
infra-bot: Created issue INF-4721 with logs and perf traces (link: https://redwood.internal/INF-4721). Please add more repro artifacts.
kevin: Patch suggestion for stability (simple, low-risk) — clamp softmax denom with eps and stable subtraction:
```
def stable_softmax(x, eps=1e-6):
    x = x - x.max(-1, keepdim=True)
    e = x.exp().clamp(max=1e20)  # avoid overflow in exp
    return e / (e.sum(-1, keepdim=True) + eps)
```
kevin: Also try short-circuit: if quant==fp8 and seq_len>512 then force kernel=paged-attn until we understand perf cliff.
anya: I'll run experiments today:
  - fixed eps=1e-3 + fp8 on
  - fixed eps=1e-3 + fp8 off (bf16)
  - disable hysteresis and compare
  - run sampling with extra kernel traces to get distribution of switchover boundaries
mike: I'll attach the perf traces and Kv-cache lock contention profiles to INF-4721. Early hint: lock contention spikes during switchover windows.
anya: TL;DR: Likely a joint numeric + scheduling problem. Immediate mitigation = conservative eps (1e-3) + opt-out fp8 for the switchover policy. We'll follow up with more data in INF-4721. @kevin @mike please add any configs/logs you used.
kevin: Ack. I'll try microbenching flash-attn-v2 kernel with deterministic inputs and 8-bit quant table tweaks.
anya: thanks team. will post results in thread and update INF-4721 when tests finish. :thumbsup:
